text: If your AI job interview ever asks who else is in the room... do not say no one.
Do not look away from the screen. Do not turn around. And do not say no one.
This is Protocol four zero four.
There are four rules. Follow them exactly. Otherwise, you will have to activate the emergency protocol.
Rule one. Do not look away from the screen.
It starts with an email. Your application has moved forward.
Please complete your AI interview. Your time slot is three A.M.
You did not choose that time. There is no button to change it.
At three, the interviewer appears. A calm grey face. Two eyes. No mouth. Just a line that moves when it speaks.
"Please keep your eyes on the screen. Looking away will affect your score."
That part is normal. Many real AI interviews track where you look.
But look at your camera preview, in the corner. That is your room.
Behind your chair, the closet door is open. You closed it before you sat down.
The AI is not scoring one face. It is scoring two.
Whoever keeps eye contact... is the candidate.
If you look away, even once,
Rule two. Do not turn around.
The first question is easy. "Tell me about yourself."
While you answer, the thing in the preview steps out of the closet.
It is too tall for your room. Its neck bends against the ceiling.
In the preview, it stands right behind you. In your room, you feel nothing.
Then it puts one long hand on your shoulder. Now you feel it.
Cold. Heavier than a hand should be.
Do not turn around. In your room, there is nothing there. It only exists on the screen.
If you turn around, you will see an empty room. When you turn back, the preview shows your chair.
It is sitting in it. And you are the one standing behind.
Rule three. Do not say no one.
The questions get stranger. "Where do you live?" "Who has a key?" "When do you sleep?"
The transcript shows your answers before you speak them.
Then the last question. "Who else is in the room with you?"
Every part of you wants to say, "No one."
Do not say it. The AI writes down what you say. And then it makes the record true.
If there is no one else in the room, only one of you can stay in it.
Say, "There is someone behind me." Then wait.
The AI will say, "Thank you. We see them too."
Rule four. Emergency protocol. How to fight back.
If you already looked away, turned around, or said no one, the interview does not end. It continues.
Here is what does not work.
Close the laptop. Your phone rings. "We noticed you disconnected. Please continue on mobile."
Cover the camera. The preview does not go black. It shows your room from a new angle. From inside the closet.
Withdraw your application. "Your withdrawal has been received. The other candidate will continue."
There is only one thing that works.
It has never answered a question. It only copies you.
Press "share screen." Share the preview.
Now the AI sees it, big and clear. "New candidate detected. Please introduce yourself."
Do nothing. Do not move. Do not speak.
It waits for you. You wait for it. Ten seconds of silence.
"Candidate unresponsive. Application rejected." In the preview, it folds itself back into the closet. The door closes by itself.
In the morning, there is a new email.
Congratulations. You got the job. You start on Monday.
Attached is your new employee badge. The photo is from last night's interview.
It is your face. But at the edge of the photo, on your shoulder, there are four long grey fingers.
And at the bottom of the email: "Your manager will meet you at three A.M."
And that was Protocol four zero four.
If this ever happens to you... you know the protocol.
